theory.overview: Greedy algorithms make locally optimal choices at each step, hoping to find a global optimum. Unlike DP which considers all possibilities, greedy commits to a choice without backtracking. Greedy works when the problem has optimal substructure and greedy choice property. Examples: activity selection, Huffman coding, Dijkstra, Kruskal's MST. This chapter covers greedy strategy, proof techniques, and classic greedy problems.

sections.title: Greedy Strategy
sections.content: At each step, make the choice that looks best locally. Never reconsider. Simple and efficient but only works for certain problems. Key properties: greedy choice property (local optimal leads to global optimal) and optimal substructure (optimal solution contains optimal solutions to subproblems). Proof by exchange argument: show any optimal solution can be transformed to greedy solution.

sections.title: Activity Selection
sections.content: Select maximum number of non-overlapping activities. Greedy: sort by finish time, always pick activity with earliest finish that doesn't conflict. Proof: picking earliest finish leaves maximum room for remaining activities. Time: $O(n \log n)$ for sorting, $O(n)$ for selection.
sections.algorithm: Sort by finish time. Pick first activity. For each subsequent, if start ≥ last finish, select.

sections.title: Huffman Coding
sections.content: Optimal prefix code for data compression. Greedy: repeatedly combine two least frequent characters into new node with combined frequency. Build Huffman tree. More frequent characters get shorter codes. Time: $O(n \log n)$ with min-heap.
sections.algorithm: Count frequencies. Min-heap of (freq, char). Repeatedly extract two min, combine, push back. Build tree from remaining.

sections.title: Fractional Knapsack
sections.content: Maximize value with weight limit (can take fractions of items). Greedy: sort by value/weight ratio, take as much as possible of highest ratio item. Unlike 0/1 knapsack, greedy works because fractions allowed. Time: $O(n \log n)$.
sections.algorithm: Sort by value/weight descending. Take items until full. Take fraction of last item if needed.

sections.title: Greedy vs DP
sections.content: Greedy: fast, simple, but only works for problems with greedy choice property. DP: slower, more complex, but works for problems with optimal substructure (even without greedy choice). If greedy works, prefer it. If not, use DP.

keyConcepts.name: Greedy Choice Property
keyConcepts.description: Making locally optimal choice leads to globally optimal solution. Essential for greedy correctness.
keyConcepts.proof: Exchange argument: transform any optimal solution to greedy solution

keyConcepts.name: Optimal Substructure
keyConcepts.description: Optimal solution contains optimal solutions to subproblems. Both greedy and DP require this.

keyConcepts.name: Exchange Argument
keyConcepts.description: Proof technique: show any optimal solution can be transformed to greedy solution without worsening it.
keyConcepts.method: Exchange greedy choice with optimal choice, show no worse

keyConcepts.name: Sorting
keyConcepts.description: Most greedy algorithms start with sorting (by finish time, ratio, etc.). Sorting often dominates time complexity.

steps.title: Identify Greedy Choice
steps.description: Determine what choice to make at each step (earliest finish, highest ratio, etc.).

steps.title: Sort
steps.description: Sort input by greedy choice criteria.

steps.title: Iterate and Select
steps.description: Iterate through sorted items, make greedy choice at each step.
steps.code: for item in sorted_items: if valid_choice(item): select(item);

steps.title: Verify
steps.description: Verify solution correctness (often requires proof by exchange argument).

steps.title: Return Result
steps.description: Return selected items or computed value.

practiceProblems.title: Assign Cookies
practiceProblems.description: Max children content with greed factor and cookie size.
practiceProblems.solution: Sort both, greedy two pointers. Match smallest cookie that satisfies child.

practiceProblems.title: Maximum Units on a Truck
practiceProblems.description: Max units on truck with box types (boxes per type, units per box).
practiceProblems.solution: Sort by units per box descending. Take as many as possible of highest.

practiceProblems.title: Gas Station
practiceProblems.description: Find starting gas station to complete circular route.
practiceProblems.solution: If total gas < total cost, impossible. Else, find start where cumulative never negative.
practiceProblems.hints: Check total, find start where cumulative never negative

practiceProblems.title: Candy
practiceProblems.description: Distribute candy with ratings (higher rating gets more than neighbors).
practiceProblems.solution: Two passes: left to right (if rating[i] > rating[i-1], candy[i] > candy[i-1]), right to left.

practiceProblems.title: Jump Game
practiceProblems.description: Check if can reach end of array (value = max jump length).
practiceProblems.solution: Track max reachable index. If i > max, can't reach.

practiceProblems.title: Jump Game II
practiceProblems.description: Minimum jumps to reach end.
practiceProblems.solution: Greedy BFS-like. Track current range, next range. Count jumps.

practiceProblems.title: Partition Labels
practiceProblems.description: Partition string so each letter appears in at most one partition.
practiceProblems.solution: Track last occurrence of each letter. Greedy partition when current index reaches max last seen.
practiceProblems.hints: Track last occurrence, partition at max

practiceProblems.title: Task Scheduler
practiceProblems.description: Least intervals to execute tasks with cooldown n between same tasks.
practiceProblems.solution: Count frequencies. Max frequency f, count of max freq tasks m. Result = max(len(tasks), (f-1)*(n+1) + m).
practiceProblems.hints: Max frequency and count of max

practiceProblems.title: Reorganize String
practiceProblems.description: Rearrange string so no two adjacent characters are same.
practiceProblems.solution: Max-heap by frequency. Always pick most frequent not same as previous.

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons
practiceProblems.description: Min arrows to burst all balloons (overlapping intervals).
practiceProblems.solution: Sort by end. Greedy shoot at end, skip overlapping.
practiceProblems.hints: Sort by end, shoot at end

practiceProblems.title: Non-overlapping Intervals
practiceProblems.description: Remove minimum intervals to make non-overlapping.
practiceProblems.solution: Sort by end. Greedy keep non-overlapping. Count removals.

practiceProblems.title: Meeting Rooms
practiceProblems.description: Check if can attend all meetings (no overlap).
practiceProblems.solution: Sort start and end times. Check if any start < previous end.
practiceProblems.hints: Sort start and end, check overlap

practiceProblems.title: Meeting Rooms II
practiceProblems.description: Min meeting rooms required.
practiceProblems.solution: Sort start and end times. Two pointers or min-heap for end times.
practiceProblems.hints: Sort start and end, two pointers or heap

practiceProblems.title: Car Fleet
practiceProblems.description: Number of car fleets arriving at destination.
practiceProblems.solution: Sort by position descending. Calculate time to destination. Count fleets (car behind catches up = same fleet).
practiceProblems.hints: Sort by position, calculate time, count fleets

practiceProblems.title: Boats to Save People
practiceProblems.description: Min boats to save people (each boat max 2 people, weight limit).
practiceProblems.solution: Sort weights. Two pointers: lightest + heaviest if fits, else heaviest alone.

practiceProblems.title: Advantage Shuffle
practiceProblems.description: Rearrange A to maximize advantage over B.
practiceProblems.solution: Sort both. Greedy match: if A[i] > B[j], advantage++; else, use smallest A.

practiceProblems.title: Lemonade Change
practiceProblems.description: Check if can provide change for all customers (bills: 5, 10, 20).
practiceProblems.solution: Track count of 5 and 10 bills. Greedy give change with larger bills first.

practiceProblems.title: Valid Parenthesis String
practiceProblems.description: Check if string can be made valid with '*' as '(' or ')' or empty.
practiceProblems.solution: Track min and max possible open count. Greedy update.
practiceProblems.hints: Track min and max open count

practiceProblems.title: Maximum Length of Pair Chain
practiceProblems.description: Longest chain of pairs (a,b) where b < c for next pair (c,d).
practiceProblems.solution: Sort by end. Greedy pick non-overlapping (activity selection variant).

practiceProblems.title: Two City Scheduling
practiceProblems.description: Min cost to send 2N people to two cities (N each).
practiceProblems.solution: Sort by cost difference (costA - costB). First N to A, rest to B.

practiceProblems.title: IPO
practiceProblems.description: Maximize capital with k projects (each has capital requirement and profit).
practiceProblems.solution: Sort projects by capital. Min-heap for available projects by profit. Do k times.
practiceProblems.hints: Sort by capital, min-heap by profit

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Number of Taps to Open to Water a Garden
practiceProblems.description: Min taps to water entire garden (each tap waters range).
practiceProblems.solution: Convert to intervals. Greedy like jump game II.
practiceProblems.hints: Convert to intervals, jump game variant

practiceProblems.title: Video Stitching
practiceProblems.description: Min clips to cover [0, time] interval.
practiceProblems.solution: Sort by start. Greedy extend coverage as far as possible.

practiceProblems.title: Split Array into Consecutive Subsequences
practiceProblems.description: Check if can split array into consecutive subsequences of length ≥ 3.
practiceProblems.solution: Greedy with hash map. Track counts of numbers and sequences ending at each number.

practiceProblems.title: Divide Array in Sets of K Consecutive Numbers
practiceProblems.description: Check if can divide array into sets of k consecutive numbers.
practiceProblems.solution: Sort, greedy. For each number, try to form set of k consecutive.

minigame.title: Greedy Master
minigame.description: Master greedy algorithms! Activity selection, scheduling, and interval problems.
